notes:
Longer history that actually renders, and a distiller that can say "nothing here".

Long-range views stop coming up blank. The effort matrix defaulted to a "time"
measure that only exists for days dashy watched live, so a year of history
built from your git commits had nothing to show. Past the last 30 days it now
defaults to a measure that does have that history. Picking a measure yourself
still overrides it at any range.

Better theme classification. Three things were quietly limiting it:

The daily classifier was required to name between one and four themes for
every day, so a day of tracker tidying or a dependency bump had to invent
something. It can now return nothing, which is the honest answer on those
days, and up to ten themes on a genuinely busy one.

It could not see which files belong to which theme. Those path hints were
recorded in your registry but never shown to it, so a day spent editing a
theme's own directory was often filed elsewhere.

Merge commits were being read as work. A commit whose subject is "Merge
origin/main" describes the merge, not what was done, and it was crowding out
real commits and producing themes named after the word "Merge".

The busiest days are no longer truncated. Only the first 20 commits and 30
edited files of a day were ever considered, which cut exactly the days with
the most going on. Now 60 of each.

New: "dashy theme-backfill --redistill" re-derives days that already have an
answer, for re-running a whole history on a better model or after your theme
registry has gained entries that did not exist when those days were first
classified.
